title: Sermones (Incertus)
author: Isidorus Hispalensis
source: Translated by Claude from tmp1436.tmp1436.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

passages.original: i. Veni, domine Jesu Christe Redemptor noster, qui æqualem potestatem cum Patre habes. Veni, et contere caput draconis magni; et die nobis quid es, quomodo Arius iste aliud docet quam es. Die, die, audiamus, unde haereticos convincamus. Audite, fratres charissimi, quid Dominus dicat. Ego sum, inquit, via, veritas, et vita. Nemo uenit ad Patrem, nisi per me.
passages.english: 1. Come, Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer, who have equal power with the Father. Come, and crush the head of the great dragon; and tell us what you are, how this Arius teaches something other than what you are. Speak, speak, let us hear, so that from it we may refute the heretics. Hear, dearest brothers, what the Lord says. "I am," he says, "the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me."
passages.notes: "die" (three times) is read as "dic" (speak, tell), an evident scanning error. "uenit" is read as "venit". "unde haereticos convincamus" is rendered "so that from it we may refute the heretics"; the sense is that Christ's words provide the grounds for refuting them.

passages.original: qui lues cum falsis mercatoribus, falsi monachi cum falsis puellis, falsi sacerdotes cum falsis episcopis, laici similiter cum pessimis laicis. Ibi pessimæ mulieres cum intelicissimis meretricibus : omnes inenarrabilibus cruciabuntur flammis, et non habebunt requiem, nisi Dominica die resurrectionis, sicut beatus Augustinus dicit : Dominica die resurrectionis qua hora Dominus noster surrexit a mortuis mane, illæ animæ juslorum veniunt visitare sepulcra sua, et dicere : Bene va eas , bone socie quia bene egisti mecum in hoc sæculo, bonum vas, amice dilectissime.
passages.english: [...] with false merchants, false monks with false girls, false priests with false bishops, laymen likewise with the worst laymen. There [will be] the worst women with the most wretched harlots: all will be tormented in flames that cannot be described, and they will have no rest except on the Lord's day of the resurrection, as blessed Augustine says: "On the Lord's day of the resurrection, at the hour when our Lord rose from the dead in the morning, those souls of the just come to visit their tombs and to say: 'Farewell, good companion, because you did well with me in this world, good vessel, most beloved friend.'"
passages.notes: The passage opens mid-phrase: the context before ends with the broken word "ini.", and the passage begins "qui lues". This probably continues "iniqui" ("the unjust"), perhaps followed by something like "[cum iniquis]". "lues" is unclear and may be a misreading of "fures" ("thieves"), so it is left untranslated. Other scanning errors have been read as follows: "intelicissimis" as infelicissimis ("most wretched"), "juslorum" as justorum ("of the just"), and "Bene va eas" as "Bene valeas" ("farewell").
